nomen_schemes.for: The schemes a nomen may be in (spec-10 §20). `ordering` is reserved for the ordering nomen of §6.4, which is a nomen of its own and never a transliteration of another: §6.4 forbids generating one, so a res carrying none is ordered by its resolved nomen and the surface says so. `musicbrainz` carries an identifier as a nomen, which is how an identifier survives a rename.

browse_modes.for: The modes of §9.2, each with the facets its surface opens with and the facets that may bound an index too long to be one. Every mode carries the category facet, which §9.2 requires be first-class rather than one among many; the prohibition there is on category as the only axis. A mode bounds its index only where §9.2 contemplates it — People, which after credits resolve holds every credited artist — and every res a bound excludes stays reachable by search and by lateral movement (§9.4).

continue.is: the requesting principal's own resume list (§13.4)

places.is: places, as a list and as a map

time.is: a spine over time-spans, with a counted Undated bucket

facets.for: The axes a facet may be taken on. Each is a relation the catalog already holds, so a count can be computed against the current query as §9.3 requires: a facet whose count cannot be recomputed is a false statement about what selecting it will do.

category_presentation.for: Per category of spec-04 §6.3: the surface it is presented on, the address selectors that surface honours, and the presentation assets it needs (spec-10 §12.1). §12.1 carries the shape and this registry carries the values, so a category placement can record and this table omits would be presented by nothing.

podcast.primary_surface: its entity page, listing its episodes

comic_series.primary_surface: its entity page, listing its issues

video_game.primary_surface: its entity page, and no player

category_icons.for:
What identifies a category on a surface, and what the household calls it. The glyph identifies the category and the colour groups it: twelve glyphs over five hues, because colour is preattentive and good at coarse grouping and poor at carrying a dozen identities, while a glyph carries identity precisely, survives monochrome and forced colours, and reads at three metres where a hue distinction does not. The colour follows the broad class the bytes decide; the glyph carries the finer category the bytes cannot. A companion takes neither, because it is never presented as a holding and so nothing draws it.

The name is the household's word rather than a pluralized category: a person browsing says Music and Television, not Albums and Television episodes.

A category that gathers others — a podcast, a comic series — takes the stack in its members' colour, because what distinguishes it from one of its members is that it is a collection of them, and a glyph shared with its member would leave colour as the only thing telling the two apart.

seek_granularities.for: The small and large position steps §12.3's slider carries, in the unit the medium is measured along. Keyed by unit because a step is a quantity of the medium rather than of time: a reader steps by pages and a player by seconds. On a directional remote the small step is one key press, so it is the one a person repeats.

text_track_classifications.for: The classifications of §17.4. These are different products under one language label: a person who cannot hear, offered English and given a plain subtitle track, loses every cue the plot turns on. A track whose classification no container flag establishes is `unknown`, which the picker shows as unknown rather than guessing.

accessibility.for: The affordance and hazard vocabularies of §17.3. The deployment MUST NOT assert either where it has not established it, and the default is not yet examined rather than a negation, so an affordance belongs here only where something can establish it: each of these is read from a container's own stream dispositions. No hazard is establishable from bytes, so every hazard here is one a person asserts.

affordances.captions: a subtitle stream the container marks as captions
affordances.subtitles: a subtitle stream carrying translation rather than transcription
affordances.sdh: a subtitle stream the container marks hearing-impaired
affordances.audio_description: an audio stream the container marks visual-impaired
affordances.commentary: a stream the container marks as commentary
affordances.transcript: extracted text standing for the whole of a spoken recording

hazards.flashing: sustained flashing a person asserts, which no stream disposition states
hazards.loud_sound: a sudden loudness a person asserts
hazards.motion_simulation: camera motion a person asserts as causing discomfort
